tickets.subject: OW-20 standby sync stalls after redundancy failover
tickets.description: Partner escalation for Cornerstone Supermarkets on an Orion OW-20 controller running 4.8. The customer reported that after an active-standby switchover, several SSIDs prompted for 802.1X again and some clients stayed offline for about a minute before recovering. TAC reviewed the redundancy state and saw `sync state: partial` on the standby; the event log also repeated `%REDUNDANCY-4-SYNC_STALL` every 10 seconds. `show configuration database summary` showed the configuration database had grown beyond 32,768 rows, which matched the stall condition.
tickets.resolution: TAC applied the KB-4104 workaround by pruning unused AP groups, WLAN profiles, and stale guest accounts to reduce the configuration database below 30,000 rows. After the cleanup, `redundancy force-resync` completed successfully and `show redundancy status` returned a healthy sync state. The case was closed with the customer advised to keep the database below the stated threshold until the controller can be upgraded.

tickets.subject: Intermittent client reauth after standby takeovers on OW-20
tickets.description: MetroLink Telecom NOC escalated an Orion OW-20 in 4.8 after a planned failover caused voice clients to reauthenticate and some handsets dropped traffic for roughly 30 to 60 seconds. The standby came back online, but the WLAN and policy state appeared older than the active peer. TAC checked the redundancy status and found `sync state: partial`; the event log repeatedly showed `%REDUNDANCY-4-SYNC_STALL`. The configuration database summary indicated the row count had exceeded 32,768, which is consistent with the sync encoder stall seen on this release.
tickets.resolution: TAC implemented the KB-4104 workaround by removing unused configuration objects to bring the database under 30,000 rows, then ran `redundancy force-resync` during a maintenance window. Synchronization completed and the standby received current WLAN and client-policy state. The customer was advised that this is a 4.8 limitation and to plan an upgrade path when possible.

tickets.subject: OW-20 redundancy pair shows partial sync until upgrade
tickets.description: Lakeside Hospitality opened a NOC escalation for an Orion OW-20 running 4.8 after a failover test left several guest SSIDs in an inconsistent state. The customer initially suspected a bad HA link, but both peers remained reachable and the standby never fully converged after the switchover. TAC confirmed `sync state: partial` on `show redundancy status` and noted repeated `%REDUNDANCY-4-SYNC_STALL` messages in the event log. `show configuration database summary` showed the database had passed 32,768 rows, matching the known 4.8 sync stall behavior.
tickets.resolution: TAC identified KB-4104 as the cause and recommended upgrading the controller from 4.8 to 4.9, where incremental synchronization uses a 32-bit object index. After the customer completed the upgrade, a follow-up failover test showed the standby receiving the full configuration and no further sync stall events. Client reauthentication after switchover returned to normal timing.

tickets.subject: Redundancy sync stall on OW-20 after config growth
tickets.description: CivicWorks Public Agency emailed the TAC mailbox about an Orion OW-20 on 4.8 that was still serving clients, but every planned failover caused a short outage and forced some users back through login. Their note suggested a possible RF issue, but TAC saw the symptom only during redundancy events and not during normal operation. The controller reported `sync state: partial`, and the log repeatedly contained `%REDUNDANCY-4-SYNC_STALL`. `show configuration database summary` showed the configuration database had grown beyond 32,768 rows, which fits the known stall condition on this release.
tickets.resolution: TAC applied the KB-4104 workaround by deleting obsolete AP groups, WLAN profiles, and stale guest accounts until the configuration database was below 30,000 rows. A manual `redundancy force-resync` then completed without errors, and the standby matched the active configuration. The agency was advised to keep the database below the threshold until a future maintenance window allows for remediation planning.

tickets.subject: Standby on Orion OW-20 not fully catching up after failover
tickets.description: Sunset Power Authority sent a TAC mailbox message regarding an Orion OW-20 controller running 4.8. They observed that after a switchover, some wireless clients stayed connected while others had to reauthenticate, which led them to suspect a client roaming issue. TAC checked the controller and found the redundancy pair reporting `sync state: partial`; the event log also repeated `%REDUNDANCY-4-SYNC_STALL`. The configuration database summary showed more than 32,768 rows, which aligns with the incremental sync limit problem in this release.
tickets.resolution: TAC advised upgrading the controller to 4.9 per KB-4104, which fixes the incremental synchronization encoder and prevents stalls above 32,768 rows. After the upgrade, redundancy synchronization completed normally and a test failover preserved current WLAN and policy state. The customer confirmed the reauthentication delay was no longer present.
